name: Hagel
prior: Closest: garjan (Rust library, 'sounds come from physical models, including modal resonance and stochastic particle impacts', hail listed among precipitation types; a code library, not an instrument; VS: docs.rs/crate/garjan/latest, fetch blocked). Academic rain synthesis superposes drop impacts with size/speed parameters: DAFx 2004 P_169 and 'Computational Real-Time Sound Simulation of Rain' (VS: dafx.de paper-archive), Liu/Cheng/Tong physically-based statistical rain (VS: history.siggraph.org ?p=100184). RainGen (SirenFX): droplet size/rate controls, hail texture, synthesis method unstated (VS: kvraudio.com/product/raingen-by-sirenfx). Physical Audio Modus: strings/plates/rattles collide, multi-strike synced to the DAW (VS: musicradar physical-audio-modus; kvraudio modus); RipplerX/ModalDish are tunable modal plates without a stochastic exciter (VS: polarity.me ripplerx; kvraudio modal-dish). PhISEM shakers (Cook) are the stochastic-collision archetype (R: performer-kps check). Myzel: Tropfen (bubble chirps), Koerner (grain textures), Membran (one skin), Kapsel candidate (shaker). Rare: stochastic impacts on a tuned, material-selectable surface under one finger exists in a library and in papers, not in any playable app or module found (two searches, one extended).
costNotes: Native, struck: noise + BQ lowpass + WaveShaper (dead zone, oversample 'none') + BQ highpass + envelope gain + 4 BQ bandpass modes + 4 gains + Wumm osc + gain ~ 16 nodes, 6 of them biquads -> ~0.75 (idea 0.7 ok); L3 two streams and 6 modes ~1.4. Voices live 0.3-1.5 s so the steady-state budget is mild; the 24-voice build cost (0.5 ms per voice) matters more at 1/16 lanes. Measured here (M: sim/eng_hgl_sim.js): the dead-zone stream behaves as the idea hopes only after normalisation - with threshold at 2x the LP's RMS the stream gives 23 / 77 / 175 events per s at fc 90 / 300 / 690 Hz with mean event length 1.9 / 0.6 / 0.3 ms; output RMS varies 30x between threshold 1x and 3x RMS and 3x across fc, and 2.5x RMS already drops to 7 / 23 / 55 events/s. So density is set by the threshold (fixed curve) relative to the LP's RMS, which itself scales with fc: the curve must be normalised to the LP RMS per fc, or 'Korn' silently changes loudness by 20-30 dB.
soundHeld: Hagel is struck (v.released = true), so a held finger is one shower of 0.3-1.5 s and then silence - acceptable (Membran does the same) but the finger has nothing to do after the shower; 'Hoehe = Korngroesse' is only sampled at touch. The stream's events are 0.3-3 ms noise blobs, not impacts: the HP sharpens them, but amplitude variance of a dead-zone output is small, so the patter is uniform 'frying' rather than hailstones of different weight - big hail needs heavy-tailed amplitudes (square the stream, or a second dead zone) and rates below ~40/s; above ~100 events/s with mode time constants of 30-90 ms (Q 25-80) the plate rings continuously and the result is filtered noise on a pitch = Hauch with resonators, not hail on a roof. Material identity: Holz (Q 8, ~0.1 s ring) is nearly unpitched - a thud; Glas (ratios to 6.63 f, Q 80) is a pitched tinkle that aliases nothing but turns shrill above f ~ 400 Hz; Blech with the assumed 1:1.58:2.3:3.1 ratios is near Glocke/Gong and must keep T60 < 0.8 s as the idea says. The Wumm (sine f/2, 60 ms) is the only thing that gives low notes weight. Pitch identity = Nachklang; at Nachklang 0.5 the note is audible on Blech/Glas, barely on Holz.
soundBurst: This is where it lives: a Puls hit IS the design (one shower, decayMul scales Schauer), 1/16 on Blech with Hoehe wandering through grain sizes is a believable roof rhythm, and Sporenregen/Rassel make it ice rain. Risks: identical showers per hit (seed the LP cutoff/threshold with small per-hit jitter), and at 1/16 with Schauer 0.35 s the showers overlap into a continuous hiss on the lane - cap Schauer by the step length.
failureModes: Dead-zone level and density depend on LP RMS (fc) and the fixed curve: 20-30 dB loudness swing across Korn unless normalised per fc (M).
Uniform patter: small amplitude variance -> frying, not hailstones; needs heavy-tailed event amplitudes and rates < ~40/s for 'big grain'.
Dense stream + Q 25-80 modes = continuous ringing = Hauch-with-resonators, hail identity lost above ~100 events/s.
Holz is almost unpitched (Q 8); Glas shrill above f ~ 400 Hz (6.63 f); Blech drifts into Glocke/Gong territory.
Held note has nothing to do after the shower (struck engine); Hoehe sampled once.
Overlapping showers on fast lanes merge into hiss; identical hits without per-hit jitter.
Assumed Blech mode ratios (A) and Q values need a listening pass; no measurement.
verdict: Rare: stochastic impacts on a tuned surface exist in the garjan library and in DAFx/SIGGRAPH rain papers, RainGen and Modus come close from two sides, but nothing playable puts grain size and a Blech/Holz/Glas plate under a finger. Native at ~0.75 / 1.4 with no worklet. The sim shows the dead-zone stream needs per-fc normalisation (30x level swing) and heavy-tailed amplitudes before it sounds like hail rather than frying, and the dense setting turns the plate into Hauch with resonators. As a Puls engine it is right at home; as a held engine it is a one-shot. Build it as a struck/lane engine with the stream normalised and 'Korn' mapped to rate AND amplitude spread, not only to filter cutoffs.
